CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the efficacy of current medications and management strategies for anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms, with a particular emphasis on recent adjustments to the treatment plan.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a slight improvement in his overall condition. He states that his sleep duration has increased to an average of 7 hours per night, although he continues to experience awakenings around 3 AM. He acknowledges that the combination of trazodone and melatonin appears to have contributed positively to his sleep quality, albeit with residual feelings of grogginess in the morning.
In regard to his persistent fatigue, Mr. Smith describes a modest improvement in energy levels, particularly on days when he engages in physical activity. However, he still experiences significant fatigue during high-stress periods at work. He reports that his headaches have decreased in frequency to 1-2 episodes per week, but he notes that the intensity remains moderate, rating them 4-6 out of 10. He continues to manage these headaches with ibuprofen 400 mg as needed, with no adverse gastrointestinal effects reported.
Mr. Smith expresses gratitude for the positive impact of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) on his anxiety management. He has been diligently practicing mindfulness techniques and finds that they help mitigate his anxious thoughts, particularly during work hours. He remains committed to his holistic practices, including regular yoga sessions and acupuncture treatments.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (stable usage) 6. Amitriptyline 40 mg nightly 7. Topiramate 50 mg daily 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued dosage)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where he actively employs stress reduction techniques learned in therapy. His participation in a local running group has become a vital outlet for stress relief, and he reports feeling more energized and focused as a result. He maintains a balanced diet, abstains from alcohol, and has reduced caffeine intake to improve sleep quality.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep quality has improved; anxiety remains manageable; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency has decreased; intensity remains moderate; no visual disturbances or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.4F - General: Alert, oriented, appears less fatigued compared to previous visit. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable and engaged.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Lorazepam remains at 1 mg as needed, with ongoing monitoring for potential dependency. Reinforce the importance of CBT sessions and mindfulness practices. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg; maintain melatonin at 10 mg. Schedule a sleep study if sleep issues persist beyond the next month. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 40 mg nightly and topiramate at 50 mg daily. Due to the reduction in headache frequency, no change in dosage is warranted at this time, but reassess in one month. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued engagement in physical activity and mindfulness practices. Discuss the potential for referral to a sleep specialist if fatigue does not further improve with current interventions.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2029-03-01 to reassess symptoms, evaluate treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to reach out to the office sooner should he experience any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
